From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Soldato

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian soldato (“soldier”).

Noun

[edit]

soldato

  1. A member of the lowest tier of the Italian Mafia.

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
soldato
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

From French soldat, German Soldat, Italian soldato.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /solˈdato/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ato
  • Syllabification: sol‧da‧to

Noun

[edit]

soldato (accusative singular soldaton, plural soldatoj, accusative plural soldatojn)

  1. (military) soldier
    Synonyms: militisto, armeisto
    Unu soldato militon ne faras.
    One soldier does not make a war. (Esperanto proverb)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • dungosoldato
  • infansoldato
  • lusoldato
  • rajdsoldato
  • soldatejo
  • soldatigi
  • soldatiĝi

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Esperanto soldato, French soldat, German Soldat, Italian soldato, Russian солда́т (soldát), Spanish soldado.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /solˈdato/
  • Rhymes: -ato

Noun

[edit]

soldato (plural soldati)

  1. (military) soldier, trooper, private

Interlingua

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

soldato (plural soldatos)

  1. soldier, private

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Past participle of the archaic verb soldare (“to pay a soldier or military member”), from soldo (“money, military pay”). Compare Spanish and Portuguese soldado, French soldat, Romansh schuldà.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /solˈda.to/
  • Audio (IT):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ato
  • Hyphenation: sol‧dà‧to

Noun

[edit]

soldato m (plural soldati, feminine soldatessa)

  1. soldier

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bambino soldato
